title: ZIdentity API client secrets: creation, expiry, the two-secret limit, rotation and masked reads

prose.text: Secrets belong to clients whose authentication type is `SECRET`. {{secret-auth-only}}

prose.label: Creating one.
prose.text: {{expires-at-required}} {{console-secret-rules}} A secret is shown only when it is created: [[shared.oneapi.authentication:secret-shown-once]]. The API's acceptable expiry range is open {{gap:expires-at-range}}.

prose.label: Reading them back.
prose.text: Listing a client's secrets returns them masked, so only the create response carries the value: [[shared.secret-surfaces.withheld:zid-secrets-masked]] and [[shared.secret-surfaces.withheld:zid-full-only-on-create]]. {{go-secrets-array}} {{go-add-secret-raw}} The Python SDK parses that list as a single secret: [[zidentity.sdk-python:secrets-list-into-object]]. {{python-expires-at-example}}

prose.label: Rotation.
prose.text: {{two-secret-rotation}} Whether deleting a secret also revokes the tokens issued with it is open {{gap:secret-delete-token-effect}}. {{delete-unrecoverable}}

checks.do: For a lost secret, whether a new one was added (the API returns its value once) rather than read back from the list, which is masked.
Before adding a secret, how many the client already has; a third replaces the most recent one.
Whether `expiresAt` was sent as an integer epoch in seconds, not a string or milliseconds.
Rotate a client secret in this order: add the new secret, update the consumer, confirm a call succeeds, then delete the old secret. A deleted secret cannot be recovered.
Set the rotation schedule on the operator's own terms: the 90-day and yearly cadences in the legacy notes are not captured.

secret-auth-only.statement: Creating a secret for an API client applies only when the client's authentication type is `SECRET`.

expect.description:
Creates and associates a new secret with a specified API client ID. This secret can be used for authentication with Authentication Service.

NOTE: This API is applicable only when the authentication type is SECRET.

expires-at-required.statement: The create-secret body requires `expiresAt`, the secret's expiry as an integer UNIX epoch timestamp in seconds.

expect.description: The expiration time of the client secret, represented as a UNIX epoch timestamp (in seconds).

console-secret-rules.statement: In the console a secret is auto-generated and shown with its validity period; it is generated once and cannot be updated, and its validity runs from a minimum of 30 days to a maximum of 365 days.

quotes: Secret: Click Add. A key is auto-generated and displayed along with the validity period. This key is generated once, and it cannot be updated. The minimum duration is 30 days and the maximum duration is 365 days.

two-secret-rotation.statement: A client can hold at most two secrets: adding a third replaces the most recent one, so at any time there are only two.

quotes: You can add a maximum of two client secrets. If you add a third one, the new value replaces the most recent client secret. So, at any point in time, there are only two client secrets.

delete-unrecoverable.statement: A deleted secret cannot be recovered.

expect.description: Removes a specific secret associated with an API client using the Client ID and secret ID. After deletion, the secret cannot be recovered.

go-secrets-array.statement: The Go SDK's `GetSecrets` comment records that the endpoint answers with a bare JSON array rather than the paginated envelope the rest of the package uses, and that the values in it are masked, so it shows which secrets exist and when they expire, not what they are.

quotes: // GetSecrets retrieves the secrets associated with an API client.
The endpoint answers with a bare JSON array rather than
the paginated envelope the rest of this package uses, so there is no page
And the secret values are masked, so this reports which secrets
exist and when they expire, not what they are.

python-expires-at-example.statement: The Python SDK passes `add_api_client_secret` keyword arguments through as the body, and its example gives `expires_at` as the string '1785643102' rather than an integer.

quotes: body = kwargs

expires-at-range.title: Which `expiresAt` values the create-secret API accepts
expires-at-range.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the API behavior when `expires_at` is omitted or set to a past value, and the acceptable range, are not documented. The contract now makes `expiresAt` required and an integer epoch in seconds, and the console limits validity to 30 to 365 days, but no source says whether the API enforces that window, rejects a past value, or accepts the string the Python example sends.
expires-at-range.blocks: automating secret rotation through the API
expires-at-range.resolution: Omission settled by the contract (`expiresAt` is required); range and past values still open.

secret-delete-token-effect.title: Whether deleting or replacing a secret revokes tokens already issued with it
secret-delete-token-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: rotating the secret invalidates the old secret immediately for new token requests, while tokens already issued against it stay valid until they expire. The token pages list deleting or disabling the client and manual revocation as the causes of a revoked token, and say nothing about a deleted or replaced secret.
secret-delete-token-effect.blocks: planning a rotation cut-over without a service gap

propagation-delay.title: Whether a rotated client secret takes time to propagate
propagation-delay.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'A rotated client secret may not have propagated yet; wait 5 minutes and retry.' No captured source gives a propagation delay.

secret-grace-window.title: Whether an old client secret stays valid after rotation
secret-grace-window.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'The old secret remains valid for 24 hours (grace window), so both work concurrently.' The captured sources say a client holds at most two secrets (two-secret-rotation) and give no grace period.

rotation-cadence.title: Recommended rotation cadence for client secrets and JWT keys
rotation-cadence.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Rotate the OneAPI client secret every 90 days and the JWT key yearly.' These are operator recommendations; no captured source sets a cadence.
